Expert-constrained multi-label integer scorecard tuning

This experimental model independently supports multiple diagnoses. It does not select one exclusive class. Its percentages are normalized support scores, not calibrated probabilities. It is a constrained supervised optimizer, not deep learning, and no claim of novelty, clinical validity or journal acceptance is made.

Data assumptions and merging

At the project owner's direction, identical full question-and-answer blocks in source columns A/B are assumed to belong to the same patient. Fingerprints are computed before question filtering, including source values coerced by Excel. The 55 blocks merge into 50 assumed patients, five with two recorded diagnoses. All sheet labels are retained. Three conflicting ages are left unknown and flagged, not arbitrarily resolved. This identity assumption is not independently confirmed.

Worksheet membership supplies positive labels. All other labels among the seven observed diagnoses are treated as assumed negatives for this experiment, not clinically confirmed absences. Incomplete diagnosis recording can therefore bias training. Concussion and Neurological Other have no positive cases and are frozen and excluded from evaluation.

Source mappings: VMigraine → Migraine; NeuritisHypofunction → Neuritis; ScCD → Third Window; Bilateral wkns → Bilateral. Clinical review must confirm these mappings. Age and sex are not predictors.

Preprocessing

Only existing structured questions/options are modeled. Unmatched questions/options, free text, Excel dates in choice fields and conflicting single-choice answers are omitted. Hidden conditional answers and conflicting “none of the above” selections are removed consistently with browser import. No new clinical rules are invented. Source ambiguities and missing answers require reconciliation before clinical claims.

Points and constraints

Net category points are the sum of matched signed rule weights. Support is net points divided by available positive points, clipped to 0–100%. Percentages across diagnoses do not sum to 100%. Original defaults are preserved separately.

Largest-remainder rounding creates integer baselines within each category/sign group, preserving the original rounded positive totals and negative magnitudes. Every nonzero weight keeps its sign and at least one point magnitude. Pairwise one-point transfers within the same category and sign preserve those budgets exactly. Each weight stays within ±max(1, round(25% of its integer baseline)). Explicit −100 rules, zero rules, unobserved rules and categories without positive training cases are frozen after rounding.

Objective

For each evaluable diagnosis, the loss is one half the average squared distance of support from 1 in recorded-positive patients, plus one half the average squared distance from 0 in assumed-negative patients. Loss is then averaged equally across diagnoses. Add 0.002 times the mean squared displacement of weights from their integer baselines, normalized by the allowed weight radius.

A further training-only constraint prevents macro-average recorded-positive support from falling below the integer baseline and macro-average assumed-negative support from rising above it. This constraint uses unrounded support and is aggregate, not per patient or per diagnosis. Rounding can produce tiny displayed differences. It cannot guarantee improvement on new patients.

Deterministic pairwise coordinate descent visits pairs by rule index, tries −1 then +1 point transfers, and accepts strict feasible objective improvements (tolerance 10−10). It stops after no improvement or 30 sweeps. This is a local search, not a globally optimal solution. There is no softmax, mutually exclusive label, or top-1 accuracy objective.

Evaluation and development history

The deployed weights are fitted on all 50 merged patients. Three-fold exploratory evaluation refits the model separately on each training subset. Identical modeled answer profiles are also grouped into one fold even if their full source fingerprints differ. Groups are assigned deterministically, largest first, to the fold with the smallest summed label counts, then smallest total size, then lowest index. Current folds contain 17, 17 and 16 patients. Source duplicates cannot straddle folds.

Metrics report macro mean support for recorded and other diagnoses, plus balanced squared support error. These are not clinical probability calibration, sensitivity, specificity or classification accuracy. The single-label prototype was superseded after discovery of cross-sheet duplicates. An initial multi-label fit raised other-diagnosis support, prompting the aggregate constraint. These are development decisions on the same cohort; results are not untouched or preregistered validation.

No independent test set exists. Small samples, assumed-negative labels, uncertain identity, source omissions and prior model development limit conclusions. See cross-validation guidance. The app exposes per-diagnosis training and held-out support so adverse changes remain visible.

Reproduction and privacy

Run scripts/prepare_cohort.py on the private workbook, then scripts/train_model.cjs on its private cohort JSON. The private audit retains merged source IDs, labels, fold assignments and held-out scores. Public trained-model.js contains only weights, aggregate metrics, constraints and an extraction hash. Both browser panels use the same scoring implementation as training. Patient files stay local; drag-and-drop does not upload them. Existing single-label files are supported but should be replaced by the new multi-label patient files.

Publication requirements

Verify identities and labels, distinguish confirmed negatives from unrecorded diagnoses, resolve missing/ambiguous answers, obtain applicable research/privacy approvals, review prior art, lock an analysis protocol, and validate independently with uncertainty estimates and appropriate comparison models. This prototype and its reproducible method are not a completed publishable clinical study.
